questions.question: What determines comparative advantage?
choices: Lower opportunity cost of producing a good
Lower total population
A larger national land area
A stronger currency by itself

questions.question: What determines absolute advantage?
choices: Producing a good with a lower opportunity cost
Trading a good at a lower exchange rate
Producing a good with fewer inputs per unit
Exporting a good in a larger total quantity

questions.question: What are gains from trade?
choices: Only the taxes collected at a port
Benefits made possible by exchange and specialization
All revenue earned before production costs
The physical weight of traded goods

questions.question: What are terms of trade in a two-good exchange?
choices: The number of workers living in each country
The dates when countries hold elections
The total area of each trading partner
The rate at which one good is exchanged for another

questions.question: What is an export?
choices: A good or service sold to buyers abroad
A good or service purchased from abroad
A payment made only between domestic banks
A resource held exclusively for future production

questions.question: What is an import?
choices: A good or service sold abroad
A product exchanged only within one town
A good or service purchased from abroad
A government payment that produces no good or service

questions.question: In the standard trade model, specialization follows which advantage?
choices: Larger population alone
Comparative advantage
Higher prices for every product
Absolute advantage in every task

questions.question: Why can a producer with absolute advantage in both goods still benefit from trade?
choices: Absolute advantage eliminates every trade-off
Trade requires both producers to have identical productivity
A more productive producer cannot import goods
Relative opportunity costs may differ between producers

questions.question: Why does comparative advantage concern relative rather than total cost?
choices: It compares what must be forgone when resources are used for one output
It measures only the sum of all factory bills
It ignores alternative uses of resources
It depends only on the number of workers employed

questions.question: What makes an exchange rate mutually beneficial in a simple two-good model?
choices: It must equal the higher opportunity cost plus a tax
It must exceed both partners' opportunity costs
It lies between the partners' opportunity costs
It must be unrelated to production trade-offs

questions.question: Why does trade not guarantee every individual gains equally?
choices: Trade never changes employment patterns
Some workers and firms may face adjustment costs
All income is automatically redistributed equally
Every firm produces the same product after trade

questions.question: How can changing technology affect comparative advantage?
choices: It permanently removes the need to compare costs
It changes only national borders
It makes every country's production identical
It can change productivity and relative opportunity costs

questions.question: Why might complete specialization not occur in practice?
choices: Increasing costs, transport, and other constraints can limit specialization
Every producer has the same opportunity cost
Trade is possible only with complete specialization
Countries cannot produce more than one good

questions.question: How do transportation costs affect potential trade gains?
choices: They necessarily increase gains for every participant
They eliminate all domestic production costs
They can reduce the benefits available from exchange
They have no effect on delivered prices

questions.question: Why does comparative advantage not mean a country must produce only one product?
choices: The principle applies only when no trade occurs
The principle identifies relative trade-offs, not an absolute rule for all production
Every good has an identical opportunity cost
Producing several goods makes costs impossible to compare

questions.question: Ana can make 12 posters or 6 models in the same time. With a constant trade-off, what is her opportunity cost of one model?
choices: Half a poster
Six posters
Twelve posters
Two posters

questions.question: Ana gives up two posters per model; Ben gives up four. Who has comparative advantage in models?
choices: Ana
Ben
Both have equal advantage
Neither can produce models

questions.question: If one producer's cost is two posters per model and another's is four, which trading rate can benefit both?
choices: One poster per model
Five posters per model
Three posters per model
Six posters per model

questions.question: Mina uses fewer work hours than Luis for both bread and chairs. What additional information identifies comparative advantage?
choices: Only the color of their equipment
Their relative opportunity costs for each product
Only their total population
Only their customers' addresses

questions.question: Country A gives up 3 units of cloth per tool; Country B gives up 1. Which specialization follows comparative advantage?
choices: A specializes relatively in tools, and B in cloth
Both must stop producing cloth
Neither can benefit from exchange
B specializes relatively in tools, and A in cloth
